content.text: I'm submitting rewritten part prompts that keep every number, and I've added a design note.

prompts.A: A student measures the initial reaction rate of an amylase-catalyzed reaction at three levels of pH. The table shows the mean initial reaction rate (micromoles per minute) ± 2SE for each level (n = 8 replicates per level). Identify the pH level at which the mean initial reaction rate is greatest, and use values from the table to describe how the rate differs between that level and each of the other two levels.
prompts.B: Calculate the percent change in the mean initial reaction rate from pH 9 to pH 7. Show your work.
prompts.C: Using the ±2SE values in the table, determine whether the difference between the mean initial reaction rate at pH 7 and at pH 5 is statistically supported. Justify your answer by referring to the ±2SE ranges for the two levels.
prompts.D: Amylase is a protein enzyme that binds its substrate at the active site. Explain why the initial reaction rate is lower at pH 9 than at pH 7. Use data from the table as evidence and connect your explanation to the structure of the enzyme and its active site.

input.design_note: Part A now asks for one task (identify the pH with the greatest rate and support it with values), and part D requires the enzyme structure-function concept (active site, protein shape).
